newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin says France must press Algeria on democracy.
newsitem.headline: Jospin says France must press Algeria on democracy.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin, expected to be prime minister if the left wins Sunday's parliamentary election runoff, said on Thursday France should do more to promote real democracy in Algeria.

Interviewed on TF1 television, Jospin noted that while the former French North African colony was holding a parliamentary election four days after France, "they are not going to vote in sufficiently democratic conditions".
He said it was in France's self-interest, as well as the interest of the Algerian people, to use its weight to press Algeria towards greater democracy.

"If they remain in a stand-off between a harsh military regime and fanatical Islamic movements, an explosion of the tragedy which is currently bleeding Algeria is to be feared, which would obviously also have consequences for us," Jospin said.
"I have spoken out several times over the last two years to tell the French government it should weigh more heavily on Algeria in the direction of democracy," he added.

The centre-right French government has sought to avoid any political involvement in the Algeria crisis while maintaining French and international financial aid to the military-dominated government of President Liamine Zeroual.
The authorities in Algeria have at the same time sternly warned Paris against interfering in its domestic affairs.

The June 5 parliamentary poll is Algeria's first since 1992 when the authorities scrapped a general election in which the now banned radical Islamist Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a huge lead. About 60,000 people have died since then in the violence that erupted.
Moslem fundamentalist groups, accusing France of backing the country's military rulers, attacked French targets in Algeria and staged a wave of deadly bombings in France in 1995.
